title: Unearned revenue

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches a deposit received in advance as a liability until the revenue is earned; they cover revenue recognition and the income statement, not unearned revenue on the balance sheet.

draft.title: Unearned revenue
card: Unearned revenue is money received before the business has provided the goods or services. The business has the cash, but it has not yet earned the revenue.
The business owes the customer the goods or services, or a refund. So the amount is recorded as a liability, not as revenue.
On balance day, the business works out how much has now been earned. It debits Unearned Revenue (reducing the liability) and credits Revenue for that amount.
Any part not yet earned stays as a liability. It moves to revenue in a later period, when the goods or services are provided.
draft.remember: Cash received early is a liability until the work is done, then it becomes revenue.

a.q: Ben's Tutoring in Geelong receives $900 in December for lessons to be given next year. How is the $900 recorded on 31 December?
opts: As a liability, because the lessons are still owed
As revenue, because the cash has been received
As an asset, because the lessons will earn money
As an expense, because the lessons will cost time
a.why: The lessons have not been given, so the revenue is not earned and Ben's Tutoring owes the service. That makes it a liability. It is not revenue just because the cash has arrived.
a.clue: Has Ben done the lessons yet?

b.q: On 1 May, Kara's Pool Care in Bendigo receives $1 200 for 12 months of weekly cleaning. Her balance day is 30 June. What is the adjustment on 30 June, assuming the service is given evenly?
b.why: Two months of the 12 have been earned, so $1 200 ÷ 12 × 2 = $200. Debiting Unearned Revenue reduces the liability and crediting Revenue records the amount earned. The $1 000 is the part still owed, so it stays as a liability.
b.clue: Count how many months of service have been given by balance day.

a.best: As a liability, because the lessons are still owed
